summary: MaterialDNA unknown-field validation has no project-owned scan or diagnostic-retention bound: validateKnownFields walks every supplied key and appends one error string per unknown key, so an oversized hostile plain-data table can force O(N) validation work and O(N) diagnostic memory before rejection.
evidence: At exact main ae83c0ef470eb2e73d99be41fd3561ede30c40e1, src/shared/Materials/MaterialDNA.luau validateKnownFields iterates pairs(value) without a key budget and table.insert(errors, ...) for every unknown field.
The helper is used across MaterialRecipe, MaterialState, history-event and nested material-data shapes, so this is a shared validation-boundary issue rather than one caller-specific edge case.

Adjacent MaterialDNA resource fences already cap historyEvents at 32 and anomalyModifiers at 8; HG-BACKFILL-MATERIALDNA-DENSE-BOUNDS separately addresses scan order for those dense arrays and does not bound unknown-field scanning or error accumulation.
tests/materialdna_contract.luau verifies unknown-field rejection but does not exercise oversized unknown-key tables or assert a bounded diagnostic count/work classification.

Duplicate checks found no matching open/closed MaterialDNA PR, issue, or existing MaterialDNA lane for bounded unknown-field diagnostics. Static source audit only; this mining worker did not run the test suite or Studio.
recommendedAction: After HG-BACKFILL-MATERIALDNA-DENSE-BOUNDS is complete, open one source-only Hero-Gate micro-lane to impose a deterministic project-owned budget on unknown-field/schema-shape scanning and diagnostic retention. Oversized inputs must still fail closed; valid canonical encodings, hashes, IDs and schema versions must remain unchanged; regressions should cover exact budget, budget+1, huge unknown-key tables, bounded diagnostics, non-mutation, and deterministic overflow classification without relying on pairs() order for which unknown key names are retained.
